# 1 Samuel Chapter 14 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 176v-177v | **Source Image:** 1SA_014_page_001.jpg, 1SA_014_page_002.jpg, 1SA_014_page_003.jpg

---

**1** One day Jonathan, Saul's son, said to the young man who carried his weapons, "Come on, let's cross over to the Philistine outpost on the other side." But he did not tell his father.

**2** Saul was sitting on the outskirts of Gibeah, under the pomegranate tree at Migron, with about six hundred men around him.

**3** Ahijah son of Ahitub, brother of Ichabod, son of Phinehas, son of Eli, the LORD's priest at Shiloh, was wearing the priestly vest. The troops had no idea that Jonathan had gone.

**4** On each side of the pass that Jonathan intended to cross to reach the Philistine outpost, there was a rocky crag — one called Bozez and the other Seneh.

**5** One crag rose up on the north, facing Michmash, and the other on the south, facing Geba.

**6** Jonathan said to his armor-bearer, "Come on, let's go over to the outpost of these uncircumcised men. Perhaps the LORD will act on our behalf. Nothing can stop the LORD from winning a victory, whether through many or through few."

**7** His armor-bearer replied, "Do whatever your heart leads you to do. Go ahead — I am with you, heart and soul."

**8** "All right then," Jonathan said, "we will cross over toward them and let them see us.

**9** If they say, 'Stay where you are until we come to you,' we will hold our position and not go up to them.

**10** But if they say, 'Come up to us,' we will go up, because that will be our sign that the LORD has handed them over to us."

**11** So the two of them showed themselves to the Philistine garrison. The Philistines said, "Look! The Hebrews are crawling out of the holes they've been hiding in."

**12** The men of the outpost called out to Jonathan and his armor-bearer, "Come on up here — we'll teach you a lesson!" Jonathan said to his armor-bearer, "Climb up after me, because the LORD has handed them over to Israel!"

**13** Jonathan scrambled up on his hands and feet, with his armor-bearer right behind him. The Philistines fell before Jonathan, and his armor-bearer finished them off behind him.

**14** In that first attack, Jonathan and his armor-bearer struck down about twenty men in an area of about half an acre.

**15** Terror spread through the entire camp — the garrison, the raiding parties, everyone. The ground itself trembled. It was a panic sent by God.

**16** Saul's lookouts in Gibeah of Benjamin could see the enemy camp breaking apart and scattering in every direction.

**17** Saul said to the troops around him, "Call the roll and find out who has left our ranks." When they checked, Jonathan and his armor-bearer were missing.

**18** Saul said to Ahijah, "Bring the ark of God here." (For the ark of God was with the Israelites at that time.)

**19** While Saul was still speaking to the priest, the uproar in the Philistine camp kept growing louder and louder. So Saul said to the priest, "Withdraw your hand" — meaning, never mind.

**20** Then Saul and all his forces assembled and charged into the battle. They found the Philistines in total confusion, striking each other with their swords.

**21** The Hebrews who had previously sided with the Philistines and gone up with them into camp now switched sides and joined the Israelites under Saul and Jonathan.

**22** When all the Israelites who had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim heard that the Philistines were on the run, they too joined the pursuit and attacked them.

**23** So the LORD rescued Israel that day, and the battle moved on past Beth-aven.

**24** Now the Israelites were exhausted that day, because Saul had bound the troops under a solemn oath, saying, "Cursed is anyone who eats food before evening, before I have taken vengeance on my enemies!" So none of the soldiers tasted any food.

**25** The whole army entered the forest, and there was honey on the ground.

**26** When the troops went into the forest, honey was dripping everywhere, but no one put his hand to his mouth, because they feared the oath.

**27** Jonathan, however, had not heard his father put the troops under oath. He reached out the end of the staff in his hand, dipped it into the honeycomb, brought it to his mouth, and his eyes brightened.

**28** Then one of the soldiers told him, "Your father bound the army under a strict oath, saying, 'Cursed is anyone who eats food today!' That is why the men are faint."

**29** Jonathan said, "My father has brought trouble on the land. Look how my eyes have brightened from just this little taste of honey.

**30** How much better it would have been if the troops had eaten freely today from the plunder they took from their enemies! Wouldn't the slaughter of the Philistines have been even greater?"

**31** That day they struck down Philistines from Michmash all the way to Aijalon. The troops were completely exhausted.

**32** They pounced on the plunder, seizing sheep, cattle, and calves, and slaughtered them right there on the ground. The people ate them with the blood still in them.

**33** Someone reported to Saul, "Look, the troops are sinning against the LORD by eating meat with the blood in it." Saul said, "You have broken faith! Roll a large stone over here to me right now."

**34** Then Saul said, "Spread out among the troops and tell them, 'Each of you bring your ox or your sheep to me and slaughter it here, and then eat. Do not sin against the LORD by eating meat with blood in it.'" So each person brought his animal that night and slaughtered it there.

**35** Saul built an altar to the LORD. It was the first altar he had built to the LORD.

**36** Saul said, "Let's go down after the Philistines tonight. We can plunder them until dawn and not leave a single one of them alive." They replied, "Do whatever you think is best." But the priest said, "Let us consult God here first."

**37** So Saul asked God, "Should I go down after the Philistines? Will you hand them over to Israel?" But God did not answer him that day.

**38** Saul said, "Come here, all you leaders of the people. Let us investigate and find out what sin has been committed today.

**39** As surely as the LORD who rescues Israel lives, even if the guilt lies with my son Jonathan, he must die." But not one person among the troops said a word.

**40** Then he said to all Israel, "You stand on one side, and I and my son Jonathan will stand on the other." The troops replied, "Do whatever you think is best."

**41** Then Saul prayed to the LORD, the God of Israel, "Give a true answer." Jonathan and Saul were selected by lot, and the troops were cleared.

**42** Saul said, "Cast the lot between me and my son Jonathan." And Jonathan was selected.

**43** Saul said to Jonathan, "Tell me what you have done." Jonathan told him, "I only tasted a little honey from the end of the staff in my hand. And now — must I die?"

**44** Saul said, "May God deal with me severely if you do not die, Jonathan!"

**45** But the troops said to Saul, "Should Jonathan die — he who accomplished this great deliverance in Israel? Absolutely not! As surely as the LORD lives, not a single hair of his head will fall to the ground, because he acted with God's help today." So the troops rescued Jonathan, and he was not put to death.

**46** Then Saul called off the pursuit of the Philistines, and the Philistines returned to their own territory.

**47** After Saul secured the kingship over Israel, he fought against all his enemies on every side — against Moab, the Ammonites, Edom, the kings of Zobah, and the Philistines. Wherever he turned, he inflicted punishment.

**48** He fought valiantly and defeated the Amalekites, delivering Israel from the hands of those who plundered them.

**49** Saul's sons were Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchi-shua. The names of his two daughters were: Merab, the firstborn, and Michal, the younger.

**50** The name of Saul's wife was Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz. The commander of his army was Abner son of Ner, Saul's uncle.

**51** Kish was Saul's father, and Ner, Abner's father, was the son of Abiel.

**52** The war against the Philistines was fierce throughout Saul's entire reign. Whenever Saul spotted any strong or valiant warrior, he recruited him into his service.

---

## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

Chapter 14 is a masterclass in contrast between two models of leadership and faith. Jonathan acts in daring trust -- "Nothing can stop the LORD from winning a victory, whether through many or through few" (v. 6) -- while Saul issues reckless oaths, builds altars as afterthoughts (v. 35, "the first altar"), and nearly executes the son who won the battle. The phrase *cherev ish bere'ehu* ("each man's sword against his neighbor," v. 20) signals the divine panic (*cherdath elohim*, v. 15) that turns the Philistine camp into self-destruction -- a pattern seen at Midian (Judg 7:22) and elsewhere when God fights for Israel without human strategy.

The honey episode is laden with irony: Jonathan's eyes are "brightened" (*va-ta'ornah einav*, v. 27) -- the verb suggesting both physical refreshment and spiritual insight -- while Saul's oath blinds the army into sin (eating blood-meat, vv. 32-34). The Urim and Thummim silence (v. 37) is devastating: God's refusal to answer reveals that the obstruction is Saul's own folly, not Jonathan's honey. The troops' rescue of Jonathan (v. 45) is a proto-democratic rebuke of royal overreach, asserting that the man who "acted with God" (*im elohim asah*) cannot be killed by a king's rash vow.

The genealogical summary (vv. 49-52) serves as a structural hinge, formally closing Saul's "establishment" and setting the stage for his decline. The note that Saul constantly drafted warriors (v. 52) foreshadows the arrival of David -- the ultimate warrior Saul will both desire and dread.

-- PNEUMA
